name: The New Jerusalem and Eternal Glory
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ

objectives.text: Identify from Revelation 21:2-3 that God promises a holy city where he will live with his people forever
Name the things Revelation 21:4 says God will take away in the new creation, such as tears, death, crying, and pain
Identify the river of the water of life and the tree of life in the description of the city in Revelation 22:1-2
Retell in your own words God's promise in Revelation 21:5 that he is making all things new
Explain from Revelation 21:23 and 22:5 why the city needs no sun or lamp
Explain from Revelation 21:27 that those whose names are written in the Lamb's book of life enter the city
Describe what Revelation 22:3-5 says God's servants will do in the city, including seeing his face, serving him, and reigning forever
Compare the Garden of Eden in Genesis 2 and 3 with the garden city of Revelation 22, noting what is restored and what surpasses Eden
Explain what Revelation teaches about the nations bringing their glory into the city and the leaves of the tree of life bringing healing to the nations
Explain how the names of the twelve tribes on the gates and the twelve apostles on the foundations show the one people of God from both testaments
Analyze how the cube-shaped dimensions of the city connect it to the Most Holy Place of the temple
Explain how the New Testament connects the hope of the new heavens and new earth to holy living in the present
Interpret the absence of a temple in the city in light of God and the Lamb being its temple
Connect the image of the city as the bride of the Lamb to the New Testament teaching on the church as the bride of Christ
Explain the doctrine of the beatific vision as the promise that God's people will see God and enjoy him fully
Distinguish the intermediate state of believers after death from their final state in the resurrection and new creation as the Reformed confessions teach
Analyze the continuity and difference between the present body and the resurrection body using 1 Corinthians 15 and the risen Christ
Analyze whether Scripture presents the new heavens and new earth as a renewal or a replacement of the present creation
Evaluate popular depictions of heaven, such as floating on clouds with harps, against the biblical teaching of resurrected people on a renewed earth
Write a description of eternal life with God in the new creation that is grounded in and cites specific passages of Scripture
Develop an argument tracing the biblical theme of God dwelling with his people from Eden through the tabernacle and incarnation to the New Jerusalem, where God is all in all

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (golden city with God dwelling with his people, river and tree of life, all things new, no sun, no more pain, Eden comparison, healing of the nations, cube dimensions, absence of temple, bride imagery, beatific vision, scriptural description of eternal life, popular myths, resurrection body, God all in all). Merged the grade 1 river and grade 6 tree items so the tree of life is first named early and its role for the nations is explained later. Turned the vague 'construct a description of Heaven' into a cited writing task and the 'teleology' item into a traced biblical-theological argument. Added missing competencies: entry of those in the Lamb's book of life, the service and reign of God's servants, gates and foundations as one people of God, hope linked to holy living, intermediate versus final state, and renewal versus replacement of creation. Supplied verse-level Scripture and confessional anchors (WSC Q1, Q37, Q38; WCF 25.1, 32.1-3, 33.2; HC Q57, Q58) where they state the doctrine. Left judgment and the defeat of evil, the seven churches, and general OT symbolism to the sibling sub-topics.
